name: TCA9406DCUR
title: TCA9406: 2-bit bidirectional I2C/SMBus voltage-level translator, 1.65-3.6 V to 2.3-5.5 V, with output enable
summary: A two-channel, direction-free level translator for SDA and SCL. The A side runs from 1.65 V to 3.6 V and the B side from 2.3 V to 5.5 V, with VCCA no higher than VCCB. Each channel is an N-channel pass transistor with rising-edge accelerators on both sides and a 10 kΩ pull-up to each rail, so open-drain buses need no external resistors; it runs to 2 Mbps with open-drain drivers (I2C up to Fast-mode Plus) and up to 24 Mbps when both sides are driven push-pull. OE low puts every I/O in high impedance and turns the internal pull-ups off; either supply at 0 V also leaves both ports in high impedance. Packages: SSOP-8 (DCT), VSSOP-8 (DCU) and 8-ball DSBGA (YZP).

circuits.title: Typical application: 1.8 V I2C controller to 3.3 V I2C devices
circuits.description: An I2C controller on a 1.8 V rail talks to I2C devices on a 3.3 V rail through the translator. VCCA takes the 1.8 V rail with a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground, and VCCB takes the 3.3 V rail with its own capacitor to ground. SDA and SCL pass straight through; the external pull-ups on both sides are optional and sit in parallel with the 10 kΩ ones inside the part. The controller drives OE, which has a resistor to ground.

operation.text: Each channel joins its A pin to its B pin through an N-channel pass transistor whose gate sits about one threshold above the lower-side supply. Either side may drive; there is no direction control. A 10 kΩ resistor pulls each A pin to VCCA and each B pin to VCCB, giving a DC source current of some hundreds of microamps.

On each side a one-shot watches for a rising edge and turns on a PMOS transistor (T1 on A, T2 on B) that bypasses the 10 kΩ pull-up, dropping the output resistance to about 50 Ω to 70 Ω. It stays on for about 30 ns or until the input edge is 95 % complete, if that comes sooner. Before driving the line from the other side, wait for the one-shot to end; the worst case equals the minimum pulse duration in the timing requirements. Holding off avoids contention and extra dynamic supply current.

The external driver sets the sink current. Fall times, tPHL and the maximum data rates depend on the driver's output impedance and on the line capacitance; the tabled tfA, tfB, tPHL and data rates assume a driver below 50 Ω.

The capacitive load an output can lift is bounded by the 30 ns one-shot: with a very heavy load the one-shot ends before the line reaches the rail. Keep traces short so a reflection returns within the one-shot time, and count trace and connector capacitance in the load to avoid re-triggering, contention or ringing.

OE high enables the part; OE low puts all four I/Os in high impedance and also disconnects the internal pull-ups, so without external pull-ups the lines float. tdis runs from OE falling to the outputs reaching high impedance; ten is the time the one-shots need to become active after OE rises. OE is referred to VCCA and tolerates 5.5 V; it may be tied to VCCA or driven from a GPIO. Disabling cuts the quiescent current.

For a stronger pull-up, fit an external resistor between the I/O and its own supply rail; it sits in parallel with the 10 kΩ inside. Lower pull-up values affect VOL. Extra pull-ups lower the RC of a line. The internal pull-ups are off while OE is low.

Keep VCCA at or below VCCB in operation. Either supply may come up first without damage. With either supply at 0 V both ports are high impedance, with Ioff of 2 µA max. To hold the outputs in high impedance through power-up and power-down, pull OE to GND with a resistor and enable only once VCCA and VCCB are up and stable; the driver's source current sets the smallest usable pull-down.

With open-drain drivers, as in I2C and SMBus, the part runs to 2 Mbps, covering 100 kHz Standard-mode, 400 kHz Fast-mode and 1 MHz Fast-mode Plus. With push-pull drivers on both sides it reaches 24 Mbps. It suits point-to-point links; applications listed are I2C/SMBus, UART and GPIO.

The supply of the device driving the translator sets the input range: its high level must exceed the input port's VIH and its low level stay under VIL. The supply of the device being driven sets the output range.

Each supply pin gets a bypass capacitor placed right beside it and the GND pin: 0.1 µF from VCCA (pin 3) and 0.1 µF from VCCB (pin 7), each to a via into an inner ground plane. A resistor from OE (pin 6) to a ground via keeps OE low until VCCA and VCCB are powered up. Signal traces stay short so the round trip of a reflection is shorter than the 30 ns one-shot. B pins 1 and 8 run to the system side, A pins 4 and 5 to the controller side.
